problems.stem_md:
**Community Garden**

Three years ago, the empty land behind Suan Mai School was full of rubbish. Today, it is a community garden where students and neighbors grow vegetables together. The idea came from a group of Grade 10 students who were tired of seeing plastic bags blowing across the field. At first, many adults doubted that teenagers could keep the project going. However, the students organized a weekly schedule, asked a local farmer for advice, and sold their vegetables at the school market. The money they earned was used to buy seeds and tools. Now, more than forty families take part, and the garden has become a place where older and younger people share knowledge. Several other schools in the province have visited to learn how to start similar projects.

---

the students proved the adults wrong
the students will become farmers in the future
the adults helped the students every week

problems.stem_md:
**Sleep and Learning**

Many teenagers believe that staying up late to study will help them get better grades. Sleep researchers, however, suggest the opposite. When we sleep, the brain sorts and stores the information we learned during the day. Students who sleep less than six hours a night often find it harder to concentrate and remember facts. In one classroom activity, two groups of students learned the same list of words. One group was tested after eight hours of sleep, while the other was tested after spending the same amount of time awake. The sleeping group remembered more words. This does not mean that studying is unimportant. Rather, it shows that sleep is part of learning, not a break from it. Experts recommend that teenagers get eight to ten hours of sleep and avoid using phones for at least an hour before bed.

---

Which statement would the writer most likely agree with?

choices.md: Studying all night before an exam is not a good strategy.
Everyone needs exactly eight hours of sleep.
Students should stop studying and sleep more.
Phones are the main reason why so many teenagers today get low grades at school.

**Floating Market**

For more than sixty years, Riverside Floating Market was mainly a place where farmers sold fruit to local families. When a popular travel program featured the market in 2015, everything changed. Within a few months, weekend visitors increased from a few hundred to several thousand. Some vendors were delighted because their income doubled. Others were less happy. Dear Mr. Hansen,

I am writing to complain about the fitness app I subscribed to last month. Your advertisement promised personalized workout plans and weekly progress reports. Unfortunately, I have received the same basic plan every week, and I have not received a single progress report. When I contacted your customer service on 3 March, I was told that the problem would be fixed within two days. It has now been two weeks, and nothing has changed. Yours sincerely,
Pimchanok S.
